chunks: And as for what is in this book of what Imam Al-Ridha (peace be upon him) wrote to Muhammad ibn Sinan in response to his questions regarding causes, I have narrated it from Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa Al-Daqqaq, and Muhammad ibn Ahmad Al-Sinani, and Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim ibn Ahmad ibn Hisham Al-Maktab - may Allah be pleased with them - who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Abdullah Al-Kufi narrated to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il Al-Barmaki narrated to us, from Ali ibn Al-Abbas, who said: Al-Qasim ibn Al-Rabi' Al-Sahhaf narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Imam Al-Ridha (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الدَّقَّاقُ: Al-Daqqaq (a nisba indicating a profession or origin, here part of the narrator's name)
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Ridha (a title of Imam Ali ibn Musa, often used interchangeably with Al-Reza)
key_terms.الْعِلَلِ: Al-'Ilal (causes, reasons, or underlying grounds for rulings)
key_terms.الْمَكْتِبِ: Al-Maktab (meaning 'the scribe' or 'the writer', a title for Muhammad ibn Ibrahim)
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ سِنَانٍ: Muhammad ibn Sinan, a prominent companion and scribe of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the source and transmission chain for Imam Al-Ridha's written response to Muhammad ibn Sinan?
ai.summary: This passage provides a critical isnad verification for Imam Al-Ridha’s (as) epistle to Muhammad ibn Sinan, highlighting the scholarly rigor of Shaykh al-Saduq in preserving the transmission of 'al-lil' (causes/reasons) through trusted narrators like Al-Duqqaq and Al-Sanani. It underscores the Shia tradition of valuing written correspondence as a primary source of jurisprudential and theological knowledge, ensuring the authenticity of the Imam's explanations on divine wisdom and causality.
